page.title: Composer
page.purpose: Let an operator or an agent author a generated document as a spec — content and intent, never presentation — see it rendered live under the active template, and change it by talking to an agent that has exactly the capability an external agent has.

priorities.statement: The spec is visibly the thing being edited; the preview is visibly the thing being produced.
priorities.notes: The write spine's authority rule is that the spec is authoritative and rendered bytes are a derivation of it. If the UI makes the preview feel like the document, users will ask for byte-level edits and the whole reproducibility story dies at the interaction layer.

priorities.statement: Whether a block is sourced or authored is visible on the block, never behind a click.
priorities.notes: Unsourced content is allowed by design — a pitch deck is mostly operator voice. It must never be invisible, because the difference between a cited figure and a remembered one is the difference between a report and a guess.

priorities.statement: The document's deviations from its template are listed, not implied.
priorities.notes: Every override is a bet against future template changes. A corpus where most documents carry overrides has silently lost switchability.

priorities.statement: Anything the agent chat can do, a command can do.
priorities.notes: Parity is the requirement. The chat composes public verbs; it is a client, not a privileged surface.

priorities.statement: Where the agent's reasoning ran is as visible here as where a parse ran is in the Corpus.
priorities.notes: A chat turn on a confidential document routes through the same choke point and fails closed identically. The claim that nothing left the machine has to be checkable in the surface where the talking happens.

states.description: A spec is open beside its live preview under the active template, with per-block provenance and the override list visible.
No spec exists yet; the primary action is creating one, which requires choosing a template.
An agent turn is in flight; the locality of the inference is shown while it runs, not after.
The agent has proposed a change whose blast radius exceeds this document — a template edit, or a corpus-scoped action — and is waiting for a human decision.
A render is in flight for the selected target.
Bytes were produced but a desirable fidelity was unavailable; what was skipped is named per element.
One or more source bindings could not be re-resolved; the prior snapshotted values are still shown and marked stale.
A render or mutation failed and the reason names which of the six terminal states applies.

elements.name: Spec blocks
elements.description: Content and intent per block. Each row shows whether the block is sourced or authored.

elements.name: Rendered preview
elements.description: The spec rendered under the active template for the selected target. Read-only by construction.

elements.name: Block provenance
elements.description: Sourced or authored, conveyed by text and shape as well as color.

elements.name: Render target
elements.description: Limited to targets the active template declares fidelity for.

elements.name: Refresh sources
elements.description: Re-runs source bindings and mints a new spec version. Distinct from re-rendering.

elements.name: Ask the agent to change something
Where this turn ran
elements.description: Local or remote, on the turn itself.

elements.name: Spec versions
elements.description: Append-only. Reverting to a version is how undo works.

claims.statement: The composer page exposes a named authoring region.
The spec and its rendered preview are both present, with the spec presented as the editable surface.
The preview offers no editing affordance; every change is made against the spec.
claims.rationale: DOC-P2-010. Editing rendered bytes diverges the artifact from its authority and voids reproducibility, undo and diff at once. A UI that invites byte-level editing creates pressure for a verb that must never exist.

claims.statement: Every spec block shows whether its content is sourced or authored without the operator opening it.
The sourced-versus-authored distinction is conveyed by text and shape, never by color alone.
claims.rationale: Consistent with the locality rule on the Corpus surface, and required by WCAG 2.1 AA. A reviewer checking which figures are cited cannot be asked to distinguish two hues.

claims.statement: The document's deviations from its template are listed with a count, not merely implied by appearance.
claims.rationale: DOC-P2-015. Overrides are bets against future template changes; a deviation nobody can enumerate is a switch that will fail later for reasons nobody can reconstruct.

claims.statement: Refreshing sources and re-rendering are separate actions with separate outcomes, and the surface never implies one performs the other.
claims.rationale: DOC-P2-019. Only refresh can change what the document claims. Collapsing them into one button means a restyle can silently alter a figure.

claims.statement: When a binding cannot be re-resolved, the prior snapshotted value stays visible and is marked stale rather than blanked.
claims.rationale: A refresh that silently blanked a figure would be worse than a stale one: the document still ships, and the missing number is harder to notice than a wrong one.

claims.statement: Each agent turn shows where its inference executed, while it runs and afterwards.
claims.rationale: DOC-P2-023. Chat is the newest path to a confidential document and the one a user is most likely to assume is hosted. The residency claim has to be visible in the surface where the talking happens.

claims.statement: A proposed change whose blast radius exceeds this document — a template edit, or a corpus-scoped action — is never applied without an explicit human decision.
claims.rationale: DOC-P2-024 and DOC-P2-025. Per-document overrides are cheap and reversible; template edits change documents the operator never opened, including ones already sent. The two must not feel the same in a chat window, where they read identically.

claims.statement: Undoing an agent change is reverting to a spec version, and the surface presents it that way rather than as a separate undo stack.
claims.rationale: DOC-P2-010. Spec versions are append-only, so revert-to-version is already a complete undo. A parallel undo stack would be a second history that can disagree with the first.

claims.statement: A partial render names which elements or fidelities were skipped, per element, rather than reporting generic success.
claims.rationale: The write-side equivalent of an anchor that lies. A render that quietly drops speaker notes produces a file the operator will present from.

claims.statement: Empty, populated, in-flight, awaiting-confirmation, partial and error states are all reachable and distinct.
Block navigation, the template picker, the target select, refresh and the chat input are reachable by keyboard alone.
